name: Grant programme administration (funder side)
one_line: The awarding body's own working corpus for one grant programme: the published call, the applications received from unrelated third parties, the assessment written about those applicants, the award instrument that gives money for the recipient's own purposes, and the claims and monitoring returns that flow back. It is not activated by the word grant, by a funder or agency name, or by holding a grant document; it requires the holder in the deciding-and-paying role over a bounded programme cycle. It declares no government field rows and no folder dimensions under PR-6, so activation unlocks only recognition, an applicant-protective privacy posture, universal facts, and grouping.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key_works: No canonical key names a bounded funding round run by an authority. `project` is the holder's own scoped work on the Research and Code schemas and would misread an applicant's project as the holder's. `purpose` is scoped to College Applications. `institution` names an organisation, not a cycle, and the funder here is the holder rather than a counterparty. `event` is capture-based. `record_type` is Finance-scoped. Without one such anchor no dimension can exist, because 00 requires that 'a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child' and an application reference such as CRF3-0147 is unintelligible without its programme.
proposed_fields.adjudication_note: R1c should adjudicate this together with the open question already raised on research.grants-funding about declaring a funder-carrying key, so that one decision covers both sides of the same money rather than minting two variants.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: these are template-activation signals on a fieldless schema. None of them licenses a government fact. Every accepted signal must place the HOLDER on the awarding side of the money — receiving applications and deciding them — not on the receiving side of a grant.

a call, notice of funding opportunity, or prospectus carrying an issuing-authority block plus labelled eligibility, eligible-expenditure, assessment-criteria and closing-date sections, where what the issuer offers is funding for the applicant's own purposes rather than payment for goods or services delivered to the issuer

several inbound documents authored by DIFFERENT third-party organisations, each carrying a reference token that shares one programme prefix, held on the same disk as the call that issued that prefix; the many-to-one inbound fan-in is the decisive shape and does not occur on the applicant side

an assessment artifact that scores or ranks named third parties — a scoresheet whose rows are application references and whose columns are criteria and named assessors, a moderation record, or a panel recommendation; the holder is writing evaluations ABOUT non-holders
an assessor or panel-member conflict-of-interest or eligibility declaration that names applicant organisations, signed by someone other than the applicant

an award or rejection instrument issued BY the holder, containing conditions of funding, eligible expenditure headings, a payment schedule and a recovery or clawback clause, and containing no acceptance-of-deliverables or supply clause

inbound claim, drawdown, or monitoring returns keyed to a live award reference and held alongside the award decision that created that reference, where the money flows outward from the holder and the reporting flows inward

a grants-system or portal export whose manifest member families are calls, received applications, attachments, assessments, award decisions and claims, read as a manifest without extraction: 'Compressed archives should yield their manifests without extraction'
needs_llm: deciding whether an executed instrument is a grant or a procurement contract when both name money, milestones and reporting; the discriminator is whether value flows back to the issuer as accepted deliverables (procurement) or whether the money funds the recipient's own stated purposes under conditions with recovery on breach (grant)
deciding holder role from prose letterhead and salutation when a document is a bare letter about funding and could have been written by the funder or received by the grantee
deciding whether an awarding body is an evidenced public authority or a private foundation, trust, or corporate giving programme running an identical-looking call

deciding whether a spend report on this disk is the funder's file copy of a grantee return or the holder's own report to a funder above it, when the same organisation both receives and re-grants money
never_alone: the word grant, grants, grantee, or grantor alone; it is a homograph across grant of probate, grant of planning permission, a grant deed, a land grant, and a place named Grants, and it is also the ordinary verb

a funder, agency, foundation, council, or ministry name alone; it may be issuer, counterparty, referee, cited authority, or the holder's own funder — the anchor schema already forbids an entity name as activation
an application-shaped document alone; a completed application has the same structure whether the holder wrote it or received it, and only the holder's deciding role separates the two
a monitoring, claim, or spend report alone; the identical bytes exist on the grantee's disk and on the funder's, and neither copy declares which one it is

a bare reference token such as CRF3-0147 with no issuing-authority block or call to bind it; the anchor schema already forbids a bare 4-digit number and a reference token is the same failure with more characters
award, scoring, evaluation, panel, moderation, criteria, or shortlist vocabulary alone; public procurement uses every one of those words for a different transaction
a parent folder named Grants, Funding, Awards, Applications, or Programme alone
a file extension or source_type alone; the design says to 'treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning'
a shared download session that pulled several funders' guidance in one sitting; 'A session should never be treated as proof of topic'
missing EXIF or dense OCR as proof that an image is a grants-portal screen capture; 'the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot'

work_types: call, prospectus, guidance notes, or eligibility criteria
received application, annex, or supporting attachment
eligibility check or completeness triage record
assessment scoresheet, moderation record, or panel recommendation
award decision, award letter, or rejection notice
grant agreement, variation, or conditions schedule
payment claim, drawdown, or disbursement record
closure, final report, evaluation, or recovery record
published award register or transparency return
grouping_reasons: one programme cycle, linking the call to every application received under its reference prefix, the assessment written about those applications, and the resulting decisions
one application-to-award thread, linked by an exact application or award reference carried on the application, the scoresheet row, the award letter, the agreement, and each claim
one assessment round, linking scoresheets, moderation records, declarations, and the panel meeting record without copying an applicant fact onto an assessor's file
one bounded portal export, read from its manifest, whose members stay together and stay shallow because their internal access boundaries are unknown
sparse members such as a bare annex or an unnamed scan may join a candidate group for review without acquiring an applicant, award, decision, or amount fact

template.why: Empty by contract: PR-6 leaves the government schema fieldless and a template cannot branch on undeclared fields, so an empty order is the only compliant recommendation. The world's structure stays prose: programme and cycle first, then the application or award reference, then work type, because 'For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders' and because an application reference is meaningless without the programme that issued it. Applicant and assessor names must never become branch labels — a visible folder named for an organisation discloses that it applied, and for most of the corpus that it failed. Any later order stays editable: 'The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.'

collides_with.signal: The same call, received-submission, evaluation, panel, award, and contract-management bytes occur on both sides, and the shared fixture is an evaluation scoresheet whose rows are submission references and whose columns are criteria and named assessors. The discriminator is the transaction, not the process: this row requires an instrument that gives money for the recipient's own purposes under conditions of funding with recovery on breach; procurement requires the authority buying goods or services for itself, with a specification, deliverables, and acceptance. Where only the scoresheet survives and no instrument is present, neither row activates.

The same monitoring and claim bytes exist on both disks, and the shared fixture is a quarterly claim and monitoring workbook keyed to one award reference. The discriminator is which side of the money the holder sits on: this row requires the holder to have issued the call and the award and to be receiving the return, evidenced by an issuing-authority block and the inbound fan-in; nonprofit.grant-reporting requires the holder to be the funded body reporting outward, evidenced by the funder appearing as addressee and the project being the holder's own. Neither side may activate from grant vocabulary alone.

A private foundation, corporate giving programme, or community trust runs a call, receives applications, scores them, and issues award letters with identical structure; the shared fixture is the call for applications. The discriminator is independently evidenced public-authority status for the awarding body. Where the awarding body is a private funder, the grantmaking corpus stays private-association material and this row must not activate merely because the workflow looks governmental.

Award notices, budget justifications, periods of performance, and reporting schedules appear in both, and the shared fixture is a notice of award. The discriminator is authorship and direction: this row holds the notice the authority issued to many recipients alongside the applications it received; research.grants-funding holds the single notice a principal investigator received for one project, whose organizing anchor is that project rather than a programme cycle. A funder name is decisive for neither.

also_holds_with.signal: An executed grant agreement, a variation, or a recovery notice is legitimately both a programme-administration member and a legal instrument. Coactivation is permitted; neither schema erases the other, and Legal must not be used to conclude enforceability or breach.

falls_through_to.when: a received application, an assessment or moderation record, an assessor declaration, an applicant communication, or an unsuccessful bid has no accepted programme group; disclosure that a named organisation applied, and usually that it failed, is the harm being avoided
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: a published call, award notice, transparency return, or programme guidance document has durable standalone value but no evidenced funder-side workflow on this disk
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: a readable funding-shaped artifact leaves the holder role unresolved — a bare letter about money, a planning workbook using the word Grants, or a calendar item with no bound reference
a grants-system export, database dump, or password-protected portal archive cannot be read; its filename must not manufacture a programme, applicant, or decision
another funder's guidance, a published evaluation study, or a policy paper about grantmaking was downloaded for reference with no accepted programme association

sensitivity_why: This corpus is mostly third-party material held about people and organisations who are not the holder, and most of it records failure. Received applications carry organisational and personal detail, financial position, and sometimes beneficiary data; assessments and moderation records carry scores and reasons about named applicants; declarations name relationships between assessors and applicants. Two separate firewalls apply and neither is the default posture: applicant material must not disclose assessor identity, and assessor material must not disclose applicant standing. Publicity is split within one programme — an award may be published in a transparency register while the application behind it, and every unsuccessful application beside it, is not; published award data must never lower the sensitivity of its neighbours in the same group. The design requires that privacy policy be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector, so recognition and grouping here should work from the minimum necessary excerpt or manifest, and applicant or assessor names must not appear in branch labels or group summaries.
open_question: Two unresolved items, both for R1c and Joseph. First, whether a `programme` key (or a reuse of an existing organisation key carrying the funder role) may be declared on the government schema; without it this row can recommend no dimension at all even though the world has an obvious programme-then-reference-then-work-type structure, and research.grants-funding has already raised an overlapping question from the recipient side that should be decided once rather than twice. Second, whether a re-granting body — an authority that receives money from above and awards it below — activates this row, nonprofit.grant-reporting, or both for the same programme folder; the alternatives are coactivation, a role-decided mutex, or leaving the whole re-granting corpus in Review Later until a user confirms the direction.
